content: RAG evaluation separates retrieval quality from generation quality. Context recall asks whether the retrieved context contains the evidence needed to answer the query, while context precision asks whether retrieved context is relevant and useful rather than noisy. Faithfulness or groundedness checks whether generated claims are supported by retrieved evidence; response relevancy checks whether the response addresses the user's question. Abstention evaluation should include answerable and unanswerable cases. When retrieval metrics are strong but faithfulness is weak, diagnosis should focus on the generation stage and how the model uses supplied context.
common_misconceptions: A relevant answer is necessarily faithful
High retrieval quality guarantees faithful generation

content: Evaluation metrics should reflect the cost and type of application failure. Precision matters when false positives are expensive; recall matters when missing positives is costly. Exact word-overlap metrics can be poor proxies for open-ended semantic quality. Subjective qualities can be evaluated with explicit structured rubrics or focused binary checks. Generic metrics should not be trusted blindly when they do not represent application-specific goals, though they can help identify traces for error analysis. LLM judges should be calibrated against a human-scored gold set and disagreements should be analyzed before their scores are used for consequential decisions.
common_misconceptions: One generic helpfulness metric is sufficient for every application
Word overlap reliably measures all open-ended LLM quality

content: Agent evaluation should distinguish the execution trajectory from the final outcome. A trajectory records messages, decisions, and tool calls; the outcome is the final environment or task state and is the strongest evidence that the goal was actually achieved. Reliability across repeated trials can be evaluated differently depending on whether at least one successful attempt is acceptable or consistent success is required. Complex multi-turn failures should first be localized using end-to-end task success and then debugged with step-level checks, simplified single-turn baselines, and controlled reintroduction of conversation context.
common_misconceptions: A successful-looking transcript proves the task succeeded
All valid agents must follow one exact reference trajectory

content: Production evaluation should measure both user-visible latency and economic efficiency. Time to First Token measures the delay before streaming output begins and strongly influences perceived responsiveness. Cost per successful task accounts for retries and failed runs rather than considering only one execution. Latency should be profiled stage by stage across retrieval, reranking, tools, model calls, and streaming. Cost controls include maximum-step limits, retry budgets, caching, and context summarization. Production monitoring should balance accurate evaluation with cost and latency by combining deterministic checks, sampled model-based evaluation, and human review for ambiguous or high-risk cases.
common_misconceptions: Cost of one run equals production cost per successful task
Every production trace requires an expensive LLM judge
